fragment:
The day's crypto news is a mixture of market positioning, fund flows, policy updates, and company decisions. The headlines below are worth reading for the detail behind them, not just the reaction on a price chart.

What is moving the conversation

Tether leads $15 million funding round for AI-focused payment startup Mural. The Series A round, which included participation from North Island Ventures and existing investors, brings New York-based Mural's total funding to $28 million. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Zcash developers confirm November date for upgrade that triples payment speed. The NU7 upgrade will cut the time between Zcash blocks to 25 seconds from 75 seconds. The chosen block height still has to be merged into the spec and shipped in node software. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Ripple brings Wall Street into 24/7 stock bets, but HSBC warns markets are still thin. Institutions can trade through Ripple Prime and post RLUSD as collateral. Finding enough buyers and sellers for large positions could prove harder. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Solana’s Alpenglow, its biggest network overhaul since 2020, goes live Wednesday. Alpenglow will replace the voting system Solana has used since 2020, targeting roughly 150-millisecond finality after months of testing that included a failed migration and rollback. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

A company that vouches for websites had secret keys so weak that 8 of them were cracked. Eight secret keys at eMudhra, an Indian firm that vouches for websites, were compromised. This is a generic, not crypto-specific, risk. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Bitcoin hovers around $83,000 as AI earnings revive tech, ZEC jumps 11%. Strong results from SpaceX and Super Micro sent Asian chip stocks surging, and ZEC led crypto higher after developers set a date for its next network upgrade. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Market context

Bitcoin is around $83,272 with a +2.22% 24-hour move, while Ether is around $2,455.24 with a +2.90% move. Those figures are a snapshot, not a forecast. The useful question is whether the move is supported by spot demand, volume, and a clear change in the news.

When the market is quiet, leverage and liquidity can matter as much as direction. A small headline can move price quickly when traders are positioned too closely on one side.

What to watch next

  • New ETF creations and redemptions.
  • Futures open interest and funding rates.
  • Fresh regulatory text or official statements.
  • Security warnings, outages, or custody changes.
  • Whether the reported developments become live products rather than announcements.

The fairest reading today is cautious attention. There are real developments in the industry, but none should be stretched into a guaranteed market direction.

items.title: EIP-8363: Tapered Issuance Burn - EIPs core - Fellowship of Ethereum Magicians
items.description:
US spot ETH ETFs have taken roughly $11.2 billion in cumulative net inflows, and BlackRock’s product now passes staking rewards through to holders. That demand exists because ETH became the first major crypto asset with a regulated, distributable, forecastable yield.

This proposal does two things to it. [...] Against that we are wagering the demand channel that produced roughly $11.2 billion of ETF inflows and an entry queue above 3 million ETH. One year of burn is on the order of 18% of one year of that inflow. If removing the yield costs us even a fifth of that demand, the trade is a wash. If it costs more, we have reduced the dollar value of the stake securing the chain, which is the quantity the ETH-as-money argument says it wants to protect. [...] The same pools accelerate the status-quo problem. Low-friction entry is symmetric: it is also how dilution-avoidance flows pour in at maximum speed today. The protocol churn limit still bounds actual validator-set turnover; pools shuffle claims on stake, not the stake itself.

items.title: Cryptocurrency regulation: U.S. laws and global developments
items.description: Cryptocurrency regulation is no longer a theoretical debate—it's an evolving framework that is beginning to take shape worldwide. In the United States, Congress has moved toward establishing federal oversight of stablecoins and digital asset markets. The GENIUS Act, signed into law in 2025, established a federal regulatory framework for stablecoins, while broader market structure legislation known as the CLARITY Act advanced in Congress in 2026 but has yet to become law. [...] United Kingdom. The U.K. began regulating cryptocurrency in 2020. In October 2023, the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) introduced stricter rules on crypto advertising. The Financial Services and Markets Act 2023 also expanded oversight of stablecoins. A broader regulatory framework was approved in 2026 and is scheduled to take effect in October 2027, bringing activities including crypto trading, custody, staking, and stablecoin issuance under FCA oversight. [...] Cryptocurrency regulation in the United States has historically been fragmented, with federal agencies applying different interpretations based on the nature and use of each asset. That splintered approach began to change in 2025, when Congress established a federal framework for stablecoins. Broader regulation of digital asset markets remains unsettled, although Congress and federal regulators have taken steps toward clarifying which assets and activities fall under securities or commodities

The Stablecoin Statement specifically addresses stablecoins that are designed to maintain a stable value relative to the US dollar (USD) on a one-for-one basis, [...] On December 16, 2025, the FDIC issued a notice of proposed rulemaking (the Proposal) to implement Section 5 of the Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for US Stablecoins Act (GENIUS Act). The GENIUS Act, enacted by Congress in July 2025, created a federal regulatory framework for stablecoins whereby a subsidiary of an insured depository institution could be approved to issue payment stablecoins.

Read more on Latham’s Global Fintech & Digital Assets Blog. items.description:
Regulatory trends

Stablecoin legislation

In July 2025, President Donald Trump signed the GENIUS Act legislation into law, requiring stablecoins to be backed 1-to-1 by the US dollar or other low-risk assets. The United States has also enacted the Anti-CBDC Surveillance State Act, which prohibits Federal Reserve banks from establishing or issuing a US CBDC.

SEC and CFTC crypto clarity [...] Hong Kong has introduced a dedicated stablecoin issuer licensing regime under the HKMA and FSTB. It proposes high-quality reserve-asset backing, segregation and custody requirements, independent audits, clear redemption rights, and governance standards. Algorithmic stablecoins and unbacked arrangements will face restrictions.

ETF & tokenized-asset guidelines [...] Stablecoin payment rules in the UK are still in development and have not yet come into force. The government has outlined a future framework in which stablecoins used for payments would be subject to requirements on backing, redemption, and issuer governance, with payment-system regulators gaining expanded supervisory powers over systemic arrangements. # Bitcoin, Ethereum, XRP Price Predictions Today: Why Is Crypto Falling?

Coin Gabbar

Coin Gabbar@coin\_gabbar\_·

The crypto market took a step back today. The total market cap fell to $2.76 trillion, down 0.60% in the past 24 hours. Trading volume sits at $94.41 billion.

Bitcoin slipped to $78,062.80. Ethereum eased to $2,470.13. XRP dropped to $1.38. Most coins are red today, but the drop is mild, not a crash.

### Why is Crypto Market Down Today? [...] Ethereum trades at $2,472.04 today, down 1.80%. The coin has been stuck between $2,400 and $2,550 for over a week now.

Retail selling and a slowdown in demand from bigger buyers seem to be the main reasons for the sideways action.

Near-term resistance sits around $2,520 to $2,530. That level has rejected price several times in recent weeks. Each retest without a sharp rejection tends to weaken resistance over time, which raises the odds of an eventual breakout. [...] Markets are now pricing in a 60.4% chance of a rate hike at the September 16 Fed meeting, up from 39.6% odds of no change.

A month ago, the odds were close to a coin flip. Now, the market thinks a hike is more likely than not. Higher rates usually mean less money flowing into risk assets like crypto.

### Is the crypto market in fear or greed right now?

The Fear & Greed Index shows a score of 69 today. That puts the market in Greed territory.
